title: fraiseql.toml
description: The configuration the FraiseQL compiler reads: a project configuration beside a schema document, or a schema authored in TOML.

database.description:
Database connection pool configuration (optional — all fields have defaults).

Supports `${VAR}` environment variable interpolation in the `url` field.

server.description:
HTTP server runtime configuration (optional — all fields have defaults).

CLI flags (`--port`, `--bind`) take precedence over these settings.

tenancy.description:
Tenant isolation strategy (`#892`).

Mirrors `[tenancy]` in a project `fraiseql.toml`, minus the prefix, and
lowers into the compiled schema's `security.tenancy` — the same place, read by the
same runtime. Before this existed, `tenancy.mode` was unreachable from this
authoring surface *and* from every `[domain_discovery]` project, because
`commands::compile` deliberately skips the project config when the compile input is
itself TOML (the two formats are not compatible). An operator wanting
schema-per-tenant had no knob at all: `[tenancy]` was an unknown field, and
`[tenancy]` was ignored.

Shares `TenancyTomlConfig` with the project-config path so there is one authoring
shape and one lowering ([`crate::config::security::TenancyTomlConfig::to_runtime`]),
not two that can drift.

inject_defaults.description:
Project-wide default injected parameters (`[inject_defaults]`, #1384), in the shape
the SDK config loaders read.

accent_insensitive.description:
Accent-insensitive string filters (`[accent_insensitive]`): the function their
operators fold through. Absent, the `ai*` operators are neither published nor accepted.

functions.description:
Serverless-function settings (`[functions]`, #1325).

The operational half of the functions surface — where the modules live and
which dead-letter store backs dispatch. The definitions themselves are
schema, authored by an SDK; see [`FunctionsSettings`].

includes.description: Schema includes configuration for multi-file composition

domain_discovery.description: Domain discovery configuration for domain-based organization

query_defaults.description:
Global defaults for list-query auto-params.

Provides project-wide defaults for `where`, `order_by`, `limit`, and `offset`
parameters on list queries. Per-query `auto_params` overrides are partial —
only the specified flags override the defaults. Relay queries and single-item
queries are never affected.

auth.description:
OAuth2 client identity for server-side PKCE flows.

Required when `[security.pkce] enabled = true`.
Holds the OIDC provider discovery URL, client_id, and a reference to
the env var containing the client secret. Never stores the secret itself.

grpc.description:
gRPC transport configuration.

`CompiledSchema.grpc_config` gates the server's entire gRPC transport, and its own
doc comment said it was "compiled from `[grpc]` in `fraiseql.toml`" — but no compile
path could produce it, and `TomlSchema` is `deny_unknown_fields`, so following that
documentation failed with "unknown field `grpc`". Removing the section compiled, and
the server then silently never mounted gRPC: there was no supported way to turn on a
shipped, e2e-tested transport (#780).

Reuses the compiled type directly rather than defining a TOML mirror, so the two
cannot drift the way the REST pair did.

changelog.description:
Changelog GraphQL-exposure configuration.

When `[changelog] expose = true`, the compiler injects the observer
entity-change-log (`EntityChangeLog` / `TransportCheckpoint`) types plus
their cursor query, point-lookup query, and checkpoint upsert mutation.
Requires `[observers]` to be enabled. Absent by default.

naming.description: `[naming]`: the GraphQL surface's naming convention and casing acronyms.

cost_weights.description:
`[cost_weights]`: per-operation `@cost` weight overrides, root query or mutation
name → manual cost weight, consulted by the runtime per-tenant cost-budget check.

crud.description:
CRUD function naming config for automatic `sql_source` resolution.

When set, mutations that omit `sql_source` have their PostgreSQL function
name resolved at compile time using the configured template and the entity
name derived from `return_type`.

Example:
```toml
[crud]
function_schema = "app"
function_naming = "trinity"
```

hierarchies.description:
Hierarchy definitions for ID-based ltree operators (`descendantOfId`, `ancestorOfId`).

Maps a hierarchy name to its table and ltree path column. Used by the compiler
to generate subquery-based ltree WHERE clauses that resolve an entity's ltree
path from its UUID.

Example:
```toml
[hierarchies.category]
table = "tb_category"
path_column = "category_path"
```

session_variables.description:
Per-request PostgreSQL session variables resolved from the request identity.

The runtime applies each mapping with `set_config(name, value, true)` before
every query and mutation, so RLS policies can read it with
`current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)`. This is the mechanism that makes
database-layer tenant isolation work.

```toml
[[session_variables.variables]]
name = "app.tenant_id"
source = "jwt"
claim = "tenant_id"
```

The compiled-schema field has documented itself as "compiled from the
`[session_variables]` TOML section" since it was introduced; until #628 no
such section existed in either TOML format, so the only way to declare the
mapping was to hand-author `schema.json`.

Deliberately the *same* type the runtime consumes: a CLI-side mirror struct
is exactly the producer↔consumer seam that keeps dropping declarations.

ProjectMetadata.description:
`[project]`: the metadata of every `fraiseql.toml`, the compile input or the file read
beside a schema document.

name.description: Project name (`fraiseql sbom` names the component after it).

version.description: Project version (`fraiseql sbom` versions the component after it).

database_target.description:
Target database backend. Only `"postgresql"` is accepted: MySQL, SQLite and SQL
Server were removed in v2.15.0 (#374), and [`Self::validate_database_target`]
refuses them.

description.description: fraiseql.toml: `[project] description` is no longer accepted: nothing reads it

DatabaseRuntimeConfig.description:
Database connection pool runtime configuration.

The `[database]` section in `fraiseql.toml` is **optional**.  When absent,
connection parameters fall back to the `DATABASE_URL` environment variable
or the `--database` CLI flag.

Supports `${VAR}` environment variable interpolation in the `url` field:

```toml
[database]
url      = "${DATABASE_URL}"
pool_min = 5
pool_max = 20
ssl_mode = "prefer"
```

url.description:
Database connection URL.  Supports `${VAR}` interpolation.

If not set here, the runtime falls back to the `DATABASE_URL` environment
variable or the `--database` CLI flag.

pool_min.description: Minimum connection pool size.  Default: `5`, as the server file's `pool_min_size`.

pool_max.description: Maximum connection pool size.  Default: `20`, as the server file's `pool_max_size`.

connect_timeout_ms.description:
How long acquiring a pooled connection, and opening a new one, may take, in
milliseconds.  Default: `30 000` (30 s), as the server file's `pool_timeout_secs`.

ssl_mode.description:
PostgreSQL SSL mode: `"disable"`, `"prefer"`, `"require"`, or
`"verify-full"`. Default: `"prefer"`.

Reaches the connection pool through
[`postgres_tls`](Self::postgres_tls). It was previously validated here and
then dropped by `build_config_from`, so `fraiseql run` connected in
cleartext under `ssl_mode = "require"` while a typo in the same field
failed loudly — the rejected typo being the reason an operator believed the
setting was live (#824).

Unset means "whatever the connection URL says", not "prefer": a concrete
default here would override an explicit `?sslmode=require` in `url` with a
value the operator never wrote.

transaction_retry.description:
`[database.transaction_retry]`: how often a mutation's transaction runs when
PostgreSQL aborts it with `40P01` or `40001` (#1879). Absent, once. An empty table
opts in at its defaults. The server file's `[transaction_retry]`, in the same shape.

postgres_ssl_mode.description: fraiseql.toml: `[database] postgres_ssl_mode` is how the server's configuration file (the file FRAISEQL_CONFIG names) spells this setting; in fraiseql.toml write `ssl_mode`

idle_timeout_ms.description: fraiseql.toml: `[database] idle_timeout_ms` was never applied by `fraiseql run` and is no longer accepted; remove it: the database pool has no idle timeout

TransactionRetryConfig.description:
How often a mutation's transaction runs when PostgreSQL aborts it.

Absent, a mutation runs once, as it always has. A retried function runs its body again,
so an effect outside the transaction (`dblink`, `pg_background`, a sequence) can repeat:
that is why retry is opt-in. An empty section opts in, at the defaults below.

The server reads it as `[transaction_retry]`, `fraiseql run` as
`[database.transaction_retry]` in `fraiseql.toml`:

```toml
[transaction_retry]
max_attempts = 3   # the first attempt included
base_ms = 10       # the first retry waits up to this long
max_ms = 200       # no wait exceeds this
```

base_ms.description:
The first retry waits a random duration up to this many milliseconds; each later
retry up to twice the one before. Default: 10.

max_ms.description: No wait exceeds this many milliseconds. Default: 200.

ServerRuntimeConfig.description:
HTTP server runtime configuration.

The `[server]` section in `fraiseql.toml` is **optional**.  When absent,
the server listens on `0.0.0.0:8080` with no TLS, and CORS allows
`http://localhost:3000` only (suitable for local development).

CLI flags (`--port`, `--bind`) take precedence over these settings.

# Example

```toml
[server]
host = "127.0.0.1"
port = 9000

[server.cors]
origins = ["https://app.example.com"]

[server.tls]
enabled   = true
cert_file = "/etc/fraiseql/cert.pem"
key_file  = "/etc/fraiseql/key.pem"
```

request_timeout_ms.description: fraiseql.toml: `[server] request_timeout_ms` was never applied by `fraiseql run` and is no longer accepted; set `request_timeout_secs` (in seconds) in the server configuration file, the file FRAISEQL_CONFIG names

keep_alive_secs.description: fraiseql.toml: `[server] keep_alive_secs` was never applied by `fraiseql run` and is no longer accepted; remove it: the server has no keep-alive setting

CorsRuntimeConfig.description:
CORS configuration for the HTTP server.

```toml
[server.cors]
origins = ["https://app.example.com"]
```

origins.description:
Allowed origins. Empty: the server allows `http://localhost:3000` only, and
refuses to start in production.

credentials.description: fraiseql.toml: `[server.cors] credentials` was never applied by `fraiseql run` and is no longer accepted; remove it: the server never sends `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials`, so a browser app on another origin cannot send the session cookie; serve the app from the same origin as the API, or authenticate with a bearer token

TlsRuntimeConfig.description:
TLS/HTTPS configuration for the HTTP server.

```toml
[server.tls]
enabled  = true
cert_file = "/etc/fraiseql/cert.pem"
key_file  = "/etc/fraiseql/key.pem"
min_version = "1.2"   # "1.2" or "1.3"
```

enabled.description: Enable TLS (HTTPS).  Default: `false`.

cert_file.description: Path to the PEM-encoded certificate file.

key_file.description: Path to the PEM-encoded private key file.

cert_path.description: fraiseql.toml: `[server.tls] cert_path` is how the server's configuration file (the file FRAISEQL_CONFIG names) spells this setting; in fraiseql.toml write `cert_file`

key_path.description: fraiseql.toml: `[server.tls] key_path` is how the server's configuration file (the file FRAISEQL_CONFIG names) spells this setting; in fraiseql.toml write `key_file`

relationships.description:
Relationships to other types, followed by REST resource embedding (#1266).

Keyed by relationship name, like [`fields`](Self::fields), so the name is the
table header rather than a key inside it:

```toml
[types.Author.relationships.posts]
target_type = "Post"
cardinality = "OneToMany"
foreign_key = "fk_author"     # column on the child table
referenced_key = "id"         # column on the parent table
```

The name is what a client writes in `?select=posts(id,title)`. Both the code
comment on `embedding::executor::declared_key` and CHANGELOG 2.14.0 used to cite
a top-level `[[relationships]]` block instead; no such block ever parsed, and no
authoring surface of any kind existed until this one.

subscription_policy.description:
Per-row visibility for this type's subscription deliveries (#1657):

```toml
[types.Order.subscription_policy]
owner_path = "$.owner_id"      # the row's stored key
identity_field = "user_id"     # the enriched-identity field
```

type.description: GraphQL field type (ID, String, Int, Boolean, DateTime, etc.)

hierarchy.description:
Named hierarchy reference for ID-based ltree operators.
References a key in `[hierarchies.<name>]` config.

vector.description:
pgvector configuration for `Vector` and `BitVector` fields (#386, #959):
dimensions (required — bits, for a `BitVector`), index type and distance
metric. Authored as
`vector = { dimensions = 1536, index_type = "hnsw", distance_metric = "cosine" }`,
or `vector = { dimensions = 768, distance_metric = "hamming" }` for a
binary one. Reuses the compiled-schema type directly so the authored and
compiled shapes cannot drift.

vector_distance.description:
Names the vector field whose search distance this field carries (#959).
Authored as `vector_distance = "embedding"` on a `Float` field; the value
is the distance the `nearest` search ordered by.

unique.description:
Whether this field's column is unique over the type's relation.

Authored as `unique = true`. Needed to declare a **to-one** relationship
(`ManyToOne`/`OneToOne`) that joins on this field, because such an embed answers
with one object and a non-unique key would make it an arbitrary one; the schema is
otherwise refused at load. The entity identity (`id: ID`) needs no declaration —
see
[`FieldDefinition::is_unique_key`](fraiseql_core::schema::FieldDefinition::is_unique_key).

A FraiseQL type is usually a view, where the catalogue reports no uniqueness, so
this is the author's assertion about the relation rather than something the
compiler can confirm — the same standing as the ordering key in
[`PaginationOrder::Column`](fraiseql_core::schema::PaginationOrder::Column).

scoped_like_parent.description:
Declares that the scoped type this field embeds is scoped like the document that
holds it (#1737). Authored as `scoped_like_parent = true`; see
[`FieldDefinition::scoped_like_parent`](fraiseql_core::schema::FieldDefinition::scoped_like_parent).

VectorConfig.description:
Configuration for a vector field (pgvector).

This represents the configuration for a vector embedding field,
including dimensions, index type, and distance metric.

The same config describes both vector field types: for
[`FieldType::Vector`] `dimensions` counts float components, for
[`FieldType::BitVector`] it counts **bits**. Which distance metrics are
legal follows from the field type — see [`VectorConfig::validate_for`].

# Example

```
use fraiseql_core::schema::{VectorConfig, VectorIndexType, DistanceMetric};

let config = VectorConfig {
    dimensions: 1536,
    index_type: VectorIndexType::Hnsw,
    distance_metric: DistanceMetric::Cosine,
};
```

dimensions.description:
Number of dimensions in the vector: float components for
[`FieldType::Vector`], bits for [`FieldType::BitVector`]
(e.g., 1536 for `OpenAI` embeddings).

index_type.description: Type of index to use for similarity search.

VectorIndexType.description:
Index type for vector similarity search.

pgvector supports two main index types:
- HNSW: Hierarchical Navigable Small World (faster queries, more memory)
- `IVFFlat`: Inverted File with Flat compression (slower queries, less memory)

oneOf.description:
HNSW index - best for most use cases.
Pros: Fast queries, good recall
Cons: More memory, slower index builds

IVF Flat index - good for memory-constrained environments.
Pros: Less memory, faster index builds
Cons: Slower queries, requires training

No index - exact nearest neighbor search.
Only suitable for small datasets (<10K vectors).

DistanceMetric.description:
Distance metric for vector similarity calculations.

Each metric has a corresponding pgvector operator:
- Cosine: `<=>` (most common for text embeddings)
- L2: `<->` (Euclidean distance)
- `InnerProduct`: `<#>` (dot product, negate for similarity)

oneOf.description:
Cosine distance (1 - cosine similarity).
Best for normalized embeddings (`OpenAI`, most text embeddings).
Operator: `<=>`

L2 (Euclidean) distance.
Good for image embeddings and when magnitude matters.
Operator: `<->`

Inner product (negative for similarity).
Use when embeddings are already normalized and you want max inner product.
Operator: `<#>`

Hamming distance — the number of differing bits (#959).
Binary vectors ([`FieldType::BitVector`]) only.
Operator: `<~>`

Jaccard distance — `1 - |intersection| / |union|` over set bits (#959).
Binary vectors ([`FieldType::BitVector`]) only; unlike hamming it
normalises by how many bits are set, so a sparse near-match beats a
dense one.
Operator: `<%>`

RelationshipDefinition.description:
Relationship definition in TOML (#1266).

Deserialized straight into the intermediate shape; see
[`IntermediateRelationship`](crate::schema::intermediate::IntermediateRelationship) for
which key is read off which side per cardinality.

foreign_key.description: Foreign key column on the child table, e.g. `fk_author`.

referenced_key.description: Referenced key column on the parent table, e.g. `id`.

oneOf.description: Parent has many children (array embed).
Child points to one parent (object embed).
Exactly one related resource (object or null).

SubscriptionPolicy.description:
An entity's row-visibility policy for subscription delivery (#596).

Declared per entity in the compiled schema
([`TypeDefinition::subscription_policy`](super::TypeDefinition)):

```jsonc
"subscription_policy": {
  "owner_path": "$.owner_id",      // single-level path into the after-image
  "identity_field": "user_id",     // the fraiseql.enriched.* field (#539)
  "bypass_roles": ["admin"]        // roles that get full visibility
}
```

owner_path.description:
The single-level JSON path into the after-image holding the owner id
(e.g. `"$.owner_id"`). Only `$.<field>` is supported — the delivery matchers
key on a flat field name.

identity_field.description:
The enriched-identity field (in the `fraiseql.enriched.*` namespace, #539)
whose value the owner must equal (e.g. `"user_id"`).

bypass_roles.description: Roles that bypass the policy entirely (full visibility, e.g. `["admin"]`).

sql_source.description:
SQL function or procedure source.

When absent, the compiler resolves the function name from the `[crud]`
naming config using the `operation` and the entity name derived from
`return_type`. A compile error is emitted if both are missing.

input_style.description:
How the GraphQL `input` argument is passed to the SQL function:
`"flatten"` (positional columns, the default) or `"jsonb"` (the whole
input as one `jsonb` arg).

Orthogonal to `operation`: set `"jsonb"` so a backend using the
single-`jsonb`-wrapper convention can register the real DML verb and
still receive the whole input as one argument — letting the Change Spine
record the true `modification_type`. Defaults to `"flatten"`.

changelog_pre_image.description:
Whether a successful, state-changing run of this mutation also records the
changed entity's pre-image (before-state) into the Change-Spine
`object_data_before` column, sourced from an optional `entity_before` on the
mutation's `app.mutation_response`.

Set `true` to opt an audit-sensitive mutation into an inline Debezium-style
`{before, after}` on the single change event. Defaults to `false`,
byte-identical to a schema authored before this field existed.

cascade.description:
Whether this mutation exposes the typed graphql-cascade `cascade` field
on its success payload.

Set `true` to expose a typed, selection-gated `cascade` (mutation
responses carrying all affected entities per the graphql-cascade spec),
projected to camelCase and field-authorized per entity. Defaults to
`false`, byte-identical to a schema authored before this field existed.

retry_on_abort.description:
Whether the server's transaction retry policy may run this mutation's transaction
again when PostgreSQL aborts it. Set `false` for a function with an effect outside
its transaction, which each attempt would repeat. Defaults to `true`: the mutation
follows the server.

enabled.description: Enable Apollo federation

service_name.description: Subgraph service name (surfaced in Apollo Studio and the subgraph listing)

version.description:
Apollo Federation spec version string (e.g. `"v2"`).

Preferred over [`apollo_version`](Self::apollo_version); when both are set,
`version` wins. When neither is set, the runtime defaults to `"v2"`.

apollo_version.description:
Apollo federation major version (legacy integer form; `2` ⇒ `"v2"`).

Retained for backward compatibility; prefer the [`version`](Self::version)
string. Ignored when `version` is set.

shareable_types.description:
Keyless `@shareable` value types — types every subgraph may define identically.

They are not entities: no `@key`, never members of the `_Entity` union. Without
them a value type defined in two subgraphs fails composition with
`INVALID_FIELD_SHARING`.

circuit_breaker.description: Circuit breaker configuration for federation fan-out requests

extends.description:
This subgraph `extend`s an entity another subgraph owns.

Renders `extend type Name @key(...)` instead of `type Name @key(...)`, which is
how a subgraph contributes fields to an entity it does not own — the central
pattern of Apollo Federation. The compiled schema and the SDL renderer have
always carried it; this surface could not express it (#1195).

external_fields.description:
Fields owned by another subgraph and only referenced here — typically the
borrowed `@key` field of an extended entity. Rendered `@external`.

shareable_fields.description: Fields resolvable in more than one subgraph. Rendered `@shareable`.

FederationCircuitBreakerConfig.description: Circuit breaker configuration for Apollo Federation fan-out requests

enabled.description: Enable circuit breaker protection on federation fan-out

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failures before the breaker opens (default: 5, must be > 0)

recovery_timeout_secs.description: Seconds to wait before attempting a probe request (default: 30, must be > 0)

success_threshold.description: Probe successes needed to transition from half-open to closed (default: 2, must be > 0)

per_database.description: Per-database overrides (database name must match a defined federation entity)

PerDatabaseCircuitBreakerOverride.description: Circuit breaker configuration for a specific federated database/service

database.description: Database or service name matching a federation entity

failure_threshold.description: Override: number of consecutive failures before opening (must be > 0)

recovery_timeout_secs.description: Override: seconds to wait before attempting recovery (must be > 0)

success_threshold.description: Override: successes required in half-open state to close the breaker (must be > 0)

multi_tenant.description:
Declare that this schema serves multiple tenants.

Activates the subscription tenant fail-closed gate and the cache+RLS boot
gate. Both gates named this key in their own error messages while
`deny_unknown_fields` made it a compile error to set (#758).

rls.description:
Declare that database Row-Level Security isolates this schema's data.

`[security.rls] enabled = true`. Verified against the live catalog at boot.

role_definitions.description:
Field-level RBAC role definitions — `[[security.role_definitions]]` (`#897`).

`role_has_scope` is the only input to field-level access, and it consults nothing
else. Without a producer on this workflow, marking a field `requires_scope` in a
`--schema-dir` or TOML-schema project produced a schema where no role could ever
grant that scope, so every caller was denied the field with no way out but
migrating to the other compile workflow.

Shares `RoleDefinitionConfig` and its single lowering with the project-config
producer, so the two cannot drift the way #757's did.

default_role.description:
Role granted to an authenticated principal that carries none — `[security]
default_role` (`#897`).

Consulted by `can_access_scope` when the principal's role set is empty (#894).
Never reaches an anonymous request, which is classified before that point.

error_sanitization.description: Error sanitization — controls what detail clients see in error responses

state_encryption.description: State encryption — AEAD encryption for OAuth state and PKCE blobs

pkce.description: PKCE — Proof Key for Code Exchange for OAuth Authorization Code flows

api_keys.description: API key authentication — static or database-backed key-based auth

token_revocation.description: Token revocation — reject JWTs by `jti` after revocation

persisted_queries_only.description:
Force persisted-operations-only enforcement (#379).

When `true`, the runtime forces the trusted-document store into `strict` mode
(reject any non-persisted operation) regardless of `[security.trusted_documents].mode`.
Requires a configured trusted-documents manifest to have any effect.

cost_budget.description:
Operation cost budgets (#379): `per_request_max` (a hard per-operation
ceiling the executor enforces on every transport) and
`per_tenant_per_minute_default` (the rolling window seeded for tenants
without their own budget). Shares the runtime's own type so the
authoring and consuming shapes cannot drift.

service_accounts.description:
Machine service accounts, keyed by account name (`[security.service_accounts.<name>]`).

```toml
[security.service_accounts.reconciler]
secret_env = "FRAISEQL_SA_RECONCILER_SECRET"
roles      = ["reconciler"]
scopes     = ["write:Invoice"]
```

The secret is never inlined: `secret_env` names the environment variable holding
it (ADR-0018).

audit_logging.description: fraiseql.toml: `[security.audit_logging]` is no longer accepted; write `[security.enterprise] audit_logging_enabled`

RlsConfig.description:
Declaration that this deployment relies on database Row-Level Security.

Compiled from `[security.rls]` in `fraiseql.toml`. FraiseQL does not author RLS
policies — they live in the database, keyed on the session variables the runtime
sets from the request identity — so the compiled schema can only carry the
operator's *declaration* that they exist. The server turns that declaration into
a checkable claim: when a multi-tenant schema declares RLS, boot verifies against
the live catalog that policies really are in force, and refuses to start if they
are not (#762).

Before this section existed, [`CompiledSchema::has_rls_configured`] counted
`security.additional["policies"]` — a key #612 made a hard compile error — so it
answered `false` for every schema any supported workflow could produce, and the
gates that depend on it were inert (#758).

[`CompiledSchema::has_rls_configured`]: crate::schema::CompiledSchema::has_rls_configured

enabled.description: Whether database Row-Level Security is relied upon for data isolation.

RoleDefinitionConfig.description: Field-level RBAC role definition from fraiseql.toml

scopes.description: Permission scopes assigned to this role

type.description: Policy type: RBAC, ABAC, CUSTOM, HYBRID.

EnterpriseSecurityConfig.description:
Enterprise security features, compiled from `[security.enterprise]`.

One key, the one the runtime reads. Nine others (`rate_limiting_enabled`,
`auth_endpoint_max_requests`, `auth_endpoint_window_seconds`, `audit_log_backend`,
`audit_retention_days`, `error_sanitization`, `hide_implementation_details`,
`constant_time_comparison`, `pkce_enabled`) were accepted and read by nothing; the
sections that do the work are `[security.rate_limiting]`, `[security.error_sanitization]`
and `[security.pkce]`. `deny_unknown_fields` refuses them by name.

audit_logging_enabled.description: Record mutations in the audit log (default: true).

ErrorSanitizationConfig.description:
Controls how much error detail is exposed to API clients.

When enabled, internal error messages, SQL, and stack traces are stripped.

enabled.description:
Enable error sanitization (default: true).

A table written to tune the sanitizer keeps it on: with a default of `false`, a
section that set only `custom_error_message` switched sanitization off. A section
left out is not this default; the server decides it at boot.

sanitize_database_errors.description: Replace raw database error messages with a generic message (default: true).

custom_error_message.description: Replacement message shown to clients when an internal error is sanitized.

RateLimitingSecurityConfig.description:
Per-endpoint and global rate limiting configuration for `[security.rate_limiting]`.

The single shape for this section: the CLI authors it from TOML and the
server consumes it from the compiled schema, so the two cannot drift (before
#977 each side kept its own copy — with different defaults).

enabled.description: Enable the global limit (default: true, when the table is written).

requests_per_second.description: Global request rate cap (requests per second, per IP).

burst_size.description: Burst allowance above the steady-state rate.

auth_start_max_requests.description: Auth initiation endpoint — max requests per window.

auth_callback_max_requests.description: OAuth callback endpoint — max requests per window.

auth_refresh_max_requests.description: Token refresh endpoint — max requests per window.

auth_logout_max_requests.description: Logout endpoint — max requests per window (#893).

auth_otp_send_max_requests.description:
`OTP` send endpoint (`/auth/v1/otp`) — max requests per window, per client.

Each request mails a code through the operator's account, so this bounds how many
addresses one client can mail; the store's per-address cap cannot.

auth_otp_verify_max_requests.description:
`OTP` verify endpoint (`/auth/v1/verify`) — max requests per window, per client.
Bounds guessing spread across many addresses.

auth_password_max_requests.description:
Each local-password endpoint (`/auth/v1/password/{signup,login,reset,reset/confirm}`)
— max requests per window, per client and per endpoint.

auth_anonymous_signup_max_requests.description:
Anonymous signup (`/auth/v1/signup`) — max requests per window, per client. Each
request mints a guest account and a session with no credential to check.

auth_rules_enabled.description:
Apply the per-client rules on the auth endpoints.

On unless an operator writes `false`. The rules run whether or not the global
limit (`enabled`) is on, and with no `[security.rate_limiting]` section at all: an
absent section is not a decision to leave sign-in unthrottled.

failed_login_max_attempts.description:
Maximum failed first-factor login attempts before lockout.

The off-the-shelf binary performs no first-factor login of its own, so it
cannot enforce this; a value tuned away from the default is rejected at
startup in production (#356) — see the server's `failed_login_lockout_check`.

failed_login_lockout_secs.description: Lockout window in seconds after `failed_login_max_attempts` is exceeded.

requests_per_second_per_user.description:
Per-authenticated-user request rate in requests/second.
Defaults to 10× `requests_per_second` if not set.

redis_url.description:
Redis URL for distributed rate limiting.

Optional: when unset, budgets are tracked in-memory, per process. When
set, an unreachable Redis is a **boot error** in production (#770/#777
class) — the server does not silently downgrade to per-process limits.

redis_url_env.description:
The environment variable holding the Redis URL, read by the server at startup.

The compiled schema carries the variable's name, never its value; a URL holding a
credential belongs here rather than in `redis_url`. At most one of the two is set.

trust_proxy_headers.description:
Trust `X-Real-IP` / `X-Forwarded-For` headers for client IP extraction.

Set to `true` only when FraiseQL is deployed behind a trusted reverse
proxy that sets these headers. Enabling without a trusted proxy allows
clients to spoof their IP address.

trusted_proxy_cidrs.description:
CIDR ranges trusted as proxy IPs (e.g. `["10.0.0.0/8"]`).

When set and `trust_proxy_headers = true`, `X-Forwarded-For` is only
honoured when the direct connection IP falls within one of these ranges.
When omitted with `trust_proxy_headers = true`, all proxy IPs are trusted
(less secure — the server emits a startup warning).

max_buckets.description:
Maximum tracked buckets per map — a **memory ceiling, not a security control**.

The limiter keeps one token bucket per key in each of its maps (per-IP,
per-user, per-path-and-IP, per-tenant). This caps how many it holds at once,
at roughly 200 bytes each: the default 100 000 is about 20 `MiB` per map.

Reaching the cap evicts the least-recently-used of a sample rather than
refusing the newcomer (#1080/#1143), so setting it low degrades *accuracy* —
a client whose bucket was evicted starts again with a full one — and never
availability. It is a knob to size to the host, not to tune for protection.

failed_login_max_requests.description: fraiseql.toml: `[security.rate_limiting] failed_login_max_requests` is no longer accepted; it is spelled `failed_login_max_attempts`

failed_login_window_secs.description: fraiseql.toml: `[security.rate_limiting] failed_login_window_secs` is no longer accepted; it is spelled `failed_login_lockout_secs`

key_source.description: Where to source the encryption key.

KeySource.description: Where the state-encryption key is sourced from.

PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) configuration for `[security.pkce]`.

Requires `state_encryption` to be enabled for secure state storage.

enabled.description: Enable PKCE for OAuth Authorization Code flows.

state_ttl_secs.description: How long the PKCE state is valid before the auth flow expires (seconds).

Redis URL for distributed PKCE state storage across multiple replicas.

Required for multi-replica deployments; without Redis, `/auth/start` and
`/auth/callback` must hit the same replica. Requires the `redis-pkce`
