redis_url_env.description:
The environment variable holding the Redis URL, read by the server at startup.

The compiled schema carries the variable's name, never its value; a URL holding a
credential belongs here rather than in `redis_url`. At most one of the two is set.

oneOf.description: SHA-256 (required in production).
Plain (spec-allowed but insecure — warns at runtime).

enabled.description: Enable API key authentication.

header.description: HTTP header name to read the API key from.

storage.description: Storage backend: `"env"` for static keys, `"postgres"` for DB-backed.

StaticApiKeyEntry.description: A single static API key entry.

key_hash.description: Hex-encoded hash, optionally prefixed with the algorithm (`sha256:…`).

scopes.description: OAuth-style scopes granted by this key.

enabled.description: Enable token revocation.

require_jti.description: Reject JWTs without a `jti` claim when revocation is enabled.

fail_open.description:
If the revocation store is unreachable: `false` = reject (fail-closed),
`true` = allow (fail-open).

redis_url.description:
Redis URL for distributed revocation (inherited from `[fraiseql.redis]`
if absent).

redis_url_env.description:
The environment variable holding the Redis URL, read by the server at startup.

The compiled schema carries the variable's name, never its value; a URL holding a
credential belongs here rather than in `redis_url`. At most one of the two is set.

revoke_all_ttl_secs.description:
How long (seconds) a `revoke-all` epoch is retained.

`revoke-all` records a per-user epoch rather than deleting individual
tokens, so the entry must outlive every token that could have been issued
before the revocation. Once it expires a pre-revocation token would resume
working (until its own `exp`).

Unset, the server keeps it as long as a session it signs is accepted, and
at least 86400 (24h). Set, a server with `[auth_issuer]` refuses a value
shorter than that; for tokens from another issuer, set it above their
longest validity.

TrustedDocumentsConfig.description:
Trusted documents / query allowlist configuration for
`[security.trusted_documents]`.

enabled.description: Enable trusted documents.

manifest_path.description: Path to the trusted documents manifest JSON file.

manifest_url.description:
URL the manifest is re-fetched from every `reload_interval_secs`. The manifest is
loaded at startup from `manifest_path`, which an enabled store requires.

reload_interval_secs.description: Poll interval in seconds for hot-reloading the manifest (0 = no reload).

oneOf.description: Only documentId requests allowed; raw query strings rejected.
documentId requests use the manifest; raw queries fall through.

CostBudgetConfig.description:
Compiled `[security.cost_budget]` (#379).

`deny_unknown_fields`: a typo'd budget key must fail the load, not silently
leave the budget unenforced (the compiled-schema seam rule).

per_request_max.description:
Hard ceiling on a single operation's estimated cost, enforced in the
executor's dispatch for **every** transport. `None` = no ceiling.

per_tenant_per_minute_default.description:
Default rolling per-minute cost budget for registered tenants that do
not set their own `cost_budget_per_minute`. `None` = no default.

ServiceAccountConfig.description:
A machine service account (`security.service_accounts.<name>`).

The bearer secret is **never** inlined — `secret_env` names the environment
variable that holds it.

secret_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the plaintext bearer secret.

roles.description: The `run_as` ceiling — roles granted. Empty ⇒ no role authority.

scopes.description: The `run_as` ceiling — scopes granted. Empty ⇒ no scope authority.

tenant.description: Optional tenant pin. Omitted ⇒ global / NULL tenant.

static_enriched.description:
Optional server-injected `fraiseql.enriched.*` fields, the **only**
sanctioned deviation from uniform enrichment (ADR-0016 decision 6 /
ADR-0018 decision 5) — for a daemon with no natural actor row.
Server-injected, never token-asserted.

tenant_claim.description: JWT claim name that carries the tenant identifier.

runtime.description: fraiseql.toml: `[tenancy] runtime` is read from the server's configuration file, the file FRAISEQL_CONFIG names; set it there

storage_quota.description: fraiseql.toml: `[tenancy] storage_quota` is read from the server's configuration file, the file FRAISEQL_CONFIG names; set it there

TenancyModeConfig.description:
Tenancy isolation mode from fraiseql.toml.

Determines how tenant data is separated at the database level.

oneOf.description: Single-tenant deployment, no isolation machinery.
Row-level isolation via `@tenant_id` column injection.
Schema-level isolation via PostgreSQL schemas.

InjectDefaultsToml.description:
`[inject_defaults]` as written in `fraiseql.toml`: base keys at the top of the table,
`queries` / `mutations` sub-tables beside them.

A sub-table under any other name is refused by the base map, whose values must be
strings — so `[inject_defaults.querys]` is an error, not a silently ignored table (the
SDK loaders ignore it).

The table is open on purpose: a base key is a parameter name the author chooses, so no
list of keys could close it.

queries.description: Applied to queries only, overriding a base entry of the same name.

mutations.description: Applied to mutations only, overriding a base entry of the same name.

default.description: The locale a request gets when no source names an allowed one. Must be allowed.

allowed.description: Every locale the deployment serves, in canonical BCP 47 casing (`fr-FR`).

fallback.description:
Explicit substitutes, tried before truncation: `{ "fr-CA" = "fr-FR" }`. A key may be
any well-formed tag; a target must be allowed.

resolve.description: The sources, in order. Default: the `locale` argument, then `Accept-Language`.

LocaleSource.description: Where a request's locale may come from, tried in the order `resolve` lists them.

anyOf.description: An explicit request value: GraphQL `extensions.<name>`, REST `?<name>=`.

A request header. `Accept-Language` is parsed with its q-values; any other header
carries one tag.
A field of the enriched identity (`[identity.enrichment]`'s `map`).

AccentInsensitiveConfig.description:
`[accent_insensitive]`, as compiled and as loaded.

Declaring it publishes the `ai*` string operators (`aicontains`, `aistartswith`,
`aiendswith`, `aieq`, `ailike`, `nailike`, `airegex`, `nairegex`) on every string
filter, each folding both of its sides through `function`. Without it, the operators
are neither published nor accepted. The server never creates the function:
`fraiseql compile --emit-ddl` writes it, and `fraiseql compile --database` checks it.

function.description:
The `IMMUTABLE` `text → text` function both sides are folded through, schema
qualified and lower case. Default `fraiseql.unaccent`.

ObserversConfig.description:
Observers/event system configuration — the **declarative compile-time**
shape of the `[observers]` table.

This is NOT the server's runtime schema. The same `fraiseql.toml` is fed to
both `fraiseql compile` (this struct) and `fraiseql-server`; the server's
runtime tuning lives under `[observers.runtime]` (see the server's
`ObserverRuntimeSettings` / issue #342). The [`runtime`](Self::runtime)
field is declared-and-ignored here so a shared config carrying the server's
`[observers.runtime]` sub-table still compiles — the compiler does not
validate its contents; `fraiseql run` hands them to the server, which does.

enabled.description: Enable observers system

backend.description: The runtime's event transport: `postgres` (the default) or `nats`.

redis_url.description: observers `redis_url` configures nothing: the observer runtime has no Redis transport. Remove it, and select the transport in fraiseql.toml [observers] with backend = "postgres" (the default) or backend = "nats" and nats_url

nats_url.description:
NATS connection URL (required when backend = "nats", unless `nats_url_env` names
the variable holding it)

Example: `tls://nats.internal:4443`
Compiled as written, so it may not hold a credential (user info before the host):
a URL that does belongs in the variable `nats_url_env` names.
Can be overridden at runtime via the `FRAISEQL_NATS_URL` environment variable.

nats_url_env.description:
The environment variable holding the NATS URL, read by the server at startup.

The compiled schema carries the variable's name, never its value. At most one of
`nats_url` and `nats_url_env` is set.

runtime.description:
Server-runtime tuning sub-table (`[observers.runtime]`).

Not read by the compiler: owned and validated by `fraiseql-server`, and
handed to it by `fraiseql run`. Captured as an opaque value so a shared
`fraiseql.toml` that carries server runtime tuning still passes
`fraiseql compile`.

ObserversBackend.description:
The observer runtime's event transport: `"postgres"` (the default) or `"nats"`.

`"redis"` is refused with a pointer: the runtime has no Redis transport, and the
value used to compile into artifacts as the default without selecting anything.

oneOf.description: PostgreSQL `LISTEN`/`NOTIFY` over the change log.
NATS `JetStream`.

action.description: Action to perform: an observer action type, such as `webhook`, `slack` or `email`

FunctionsSettings.description:
The `[functions]` table — the operational half of the functions surface.

The split is the one `docs/architecture/config-vs-settings.md` prescribes, and
it has exactly one owner per key. The **definitions** (what fires, on what
trigger, under what authority) are schema: an SDK authors them and they travel
in `schema.json`. The **settings** here say where the modules live and which
dead-letter store backs dispatch — deployment facts that differ between a
laptop and production, and that no decorator should be able to set.

Neither half can reach into the other: a `FunctionDefinition` is
`deny_unknown_fields` and has no `module_dir` or `dlq_store` key, so a schema
cannot set a setting; and this table has no way to declare a function.

module_dir.description:
Directory holding the function modules (`.wasm`, `.js`, `.ts`), resolved
relative to the server's working directory.

Unset ⇒ the compiler emits the convention, `functions/`. The compiled
artifact always carries an explicit value, so the server can keep requiring
one and a hand-written compiled schema that omits it still fails loudly.

shared_dir.description:
The one directory a Deno function may import from, as `@shared/<path>`,
resolved relative to the server's working directory (for example
`functions/shared`).

Unset ⇒ a function imports nothing: every `import` is refused. It must be a
directory of its own, neither `module_dir` nor an ancestor of it.
`FRAISEQL_FUNCTIONS_SHARED_DIR` overrides it in production.

dlq_store.description:
Which dead-letter store backs function dispatch (#598): `"memory"` (the
default — dead-letters vanish on restart) or `"postgres"` (durable).
`FRAISEQL_FUNCTIONS_DLQ_STORE` overrides it in production.

CachingConfig.description:
Declarative result-cache rules (#623).

Rules are **lowered at compile time** onto the two compiled fields the
runtime's result cache already consumes: the named query's
`cache_ttl_seconds` (the per-view TTL map) and each trigger mutation's
`invalidates_views` (mutation-driven invalidation). Runtime enablement
remains the server's `cache_enabled`.

enabled.description:
Gate for the rules below: `true` with rules lowers them; `false` with
rules — or `true` without rules — is refused at compile time.

backend.description:
Cache backend. Only `"memory"` exists — the runtime result cache is
in-process; any other value is refused at compile time.

redis_url.description: [caching] redis_url is set, but there is no Redis-backed result cache to connect it to. Remove the key. (Redis features elsewhere — APQ, rate limiting, PKCE — are separate subsystems with their own configuration.)

query.description: Name of an existing query (compile error otherwise).

ttl_seconds.description:
TTL lowered onto the query's `cache_ttl_seconds`. A query that already
declares one (SDK/JSON-authored) is a compile error — two authoring
sources must not silently last-write-win.

invalidation_triggers.description:
Names of existing mutations (compile error otherwise) whose success
must invalidate this query's cached results; each gains the query's
view in its `invalidates_views`.

AnalyticsConfig.description:
Analytics query definitions (#624).

Each entry is **lowered at compile time into an ordinary compiled query**:
an operator-authored, compile-validated `sql_source` (a view, typically an
aggregate/materialized one) served with the SELECT list of its declared
`return_type`. No client-supplied identifier can reach `FROM` or the
SELECT list because neither exists on this path at request time.

enabled.description:
Gate for the queries below: `true` with queries lowers them; `false`
with queries — or `true` without queries — is refused at compile time.

AnalyticsQuery.description: One analytics query (#624), compiled into a list-returning view query.

name.description:
GraphQL field name. Must not collide with an existing query and must
not end in `_aggregate` / `_window` (the executor classifies those
suffixes before query resolution, so such a query would be
unreachable).

return_type.description:
Declared type whose fields form the SELECT list (compile error if the
type does not exist).

sql_source.description:
The view to serve — validated as a SQL identifier at compile time
(reject, never escape).

SchemaIncludes.description:
Schema includes for multi-file composition (glob patterns)

Supports glob patterns for flexible file inclusion:
```toml
[schema.includes]
types = ["schema/types/**/*.json"]
queries = ["schema/queries/**/*.json"]
mutations = ["schema/mutations/**/*.json"]
```

DomainDiscovery.description:
Domain-based schema organization

Automatically discovers schema files in domain directories:
```toml
[schema.domain_discovery]
enabled = true
root_dir = "schema"
```

Expects structure:
```text
schema/
├── auth/
│   ├── types.json
│   ├── queries.json
│   └── mutations.json
├── products/
│   ├── types.json
│   ├── queries.json
│   └── mutations.json
```

enabled.description: Enable automatic domain discovery

QueryDefaults.description:
Global defaults for list-query auto-params.

Applied when a per-query `auto_params` does not specify a given flag.
Relay queries and single-item queries are never affected.

```toml
[query_defaults]
where            = true
order_by         = true
limit            = false  # e.g. Relay-first project
offset           = false
pagination_order = "identity"
```

pagination_order.description:
What the compiler does about the order paginated reads are cut in (#1303).

```toml
[query_defaults]
pagination_order = "identity"  # default | "refuse" | "allow"
```

PaginationPosture.description:
What the compiler does about the order a paginated read's pages are cut in
(#1303).

An offset page is a slice of a *sequence*, and a read with no `ORDER BY` is not
a sequence — two pages of the same relation can overlap and skip rows, under a
`200`. The deployment-wide answer is here; a query overrides it with its own
`pagination_order`.

# Why all three are compile-time

#1303 framed the strict posture as a request-time `400`, because it framed the
ordering as a request property. It is not one: since the order is recorded per
query in the compiled schema, every posture resolves into what the compiler
writes there, and a second switch at runtime would be a second place the answer
lives — free to disagree with the artifact that is supposed to *be* the answer.
Refusing at compile time is also strictly earlier than refusing at request time.

oneOf.description:
Every paginating query gets the entity identity, and an author may declare
`pagination_order = "none"` to keep a self-ordering view's own `ORDER BY`.

The default, and the founder decision of 2026-09-08: the boilerplate of a
must-declare rule is a permanent tax on every paginated query written from
now on, while the identity default's cost is bounded, measured (1.7–7.7×
on unordered paginated reads) and recoverable by one declaration in the
minority of cases where it is wrong.

As [`Identity`](Self::Identity), and `pagination_order = "none"` is refused.

#1303's option 1, kept as a posture rather than a default: in this
deployment every paginated read has a total order and there are no
exceptions, including the self-ordering-view one. The refusal is a compile
error naming the query, not a `400` a client discovers.

Derive nothing: a query is ordered only where its author declared a column.

The pre-#1303 behaviour, kept because this release changes what an
unordered paginated read returns and an operator may need the old answer
while their clients catch up. It restores the defect with it — which is why
the compile warns for every query it leaves unordered.

OidcClientConfig.description:
OIDC configuration for `[auth]`.

This is the CLI's **compile-time view** of the `[auth]` block. The server
reads the same `[auth]` block independently into its own
[`OidcConfig`](fraiseql_core::security::OidcConfig) at runtime, so this
schema exists to *accept and structurally validate* the same block the
server consumes — not to lower it into the compiled schema (the compiled
schema carries no auth). Every JWT-validation field here must therefore stay
field-compatible with `OidcConfig`, or `deny_unknown_fields` would reject a
config the server accepts.

Two independent groups may be configured, together or separately:

- **JWT validation** — `issuer` **or** `jwks_uri`, plus `audience` and the rest of
  `OidcConfig`'s JWT settings (`additional_audiences`, `allowed_algorithms`,
  `jwks_cache_ttl_secs`, `clock_skew_secs`, `required`, `scope_claim`, `require_jti`,
  `[auth.me]`). The server consumes these to validate incoming bearer tokens; the CLI accepts
  them so the same file parses under both. Accepted and functional. `issuer` may be omitted for
  identity providers whose access tokens carry no `iss` claim (e.g. self-hosted Hanko); in that
  **issuer-less** mode `jwks_uri` must be pinned, since discovery cannot locate the JWKS
  endpoint without an issuer.
- **PKCE OAuth client** (server-side login) — `discovery_url`, `client_id`, `client_secret_env`,
  `server_redirect_uri`, configured all four together. **Not yet functional on the compiled path
  (tracked in #621):** the compiled schema carries no `auth`/`auth_endpoints` for the server to
  consume, so a complete client group is *rejected at compile time* rather than silently
  accepted.

At least one group must be present; an empty `[auth]` is a load error. The client
secret itself must never appear here — `client_secret_env` names the environment
variable that holds it.

```toml
[auth]
issuer   = "https://accounts.google.com"
audience = "my-api"
```

Issuer-less (e.g. Hanko), pinning the JWKS endpoint:

```toml
[auth]
jwks_uri = "https://hanko.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json"
audience = "my-relying-party-id"
```

issuer.description: OIDC issuer URL for JWT validation (e.g. `"https://accounts.google.com"`).

audience.description:
Expected `aud` claim for JWT validation. Required at runtime by the
server's `OidcConfig` to prevent token-confusion attacks.

jwks_uri.description:
Pinned JWKS endpoint for JWT validation (skips OIDC discovery).

Required for **issuer-less** identity providers — IdPs whose access
tokens omit the `iss` claim (e.g. self-hosted Hanko). With `issuer`
unset, discovery cannot locate the JWKS endpoint, so it must be pinned
here. May also be set alongside `issuer` to skip discovery.

allowed_algorithms.description: Allowed JWT signing algorithms (union-compat; the server defaults to RS256).

jwks_cache_ttl_secs.description: JWKS cache TTL in seconds (union-compat with `OidcConfig`).

required.description: Require authentication for all requests (union-compat with `OidcConfig`).

require_jti.description: Require the `jti` claim on every token (union-compat with `OidcConfig`).

additional_issuers.description:
`[[auth.additional_issuers]]` further trusted token issuers (#1400; union-compat
with `OidcConfig`). The server's own type, so the two cannot drift.

discovery_url.description: PKCE: OIDC provider discovery URL. **Not yet functional (#621).**

client_id.description: PKCE: OAuth2 `client_id` registered with the provider. **Not yet functional (#621).**

client_secret_env.description:
PKCE: name of the environment variable that holds the client secret.
The secret itself must never appear in TOML or the compiled schema.
**Not yet functional (#621).**

server_redirect_uri.description:
PKCE: the full URL of this server's `/auth/callback` endpoint.
**Not yet functional (#621).**

social.description:
Social-login providers (`[auth.social.google]` / `[auth.social.github]`,
#368). Deserializes directly into the **compiled** type so the authored
and compiled shapes cannot drift; the merger embeds it verbatim under
the compiled `auth.social` object. An unimplemented provider key
(`apple`, `discord`, …) is an unknown-field load error, not a
silently-ignored table.

local.description:
First-party auth methods the server operates itself (`[auth.local]`,
#367): email+password, email `OTP`/magic link, `TOTP` `MFA`, anonymous
guest sessions. Deserializes directly into the compiled type so the
authored and compiled shapes cannot drift.

session.description:
How long the sessions the server mints last, and whether they can be refreshed
(`[auth.session]`, #1853). Deserializes directly into the compiled type.

database.description:
The database first-party auth connects to, as its own role (`[auth.database]`,
#1965). Deserializes directly into the compiled type.

MeEndpointConfig.description:
Configuration for the `GET /auth/me` session-identity endpoint.

Exposed at `/auth/me` when enabled.  The endpoint reads the validated
JWT already in the request context and returns a JSON object containing
`sub`, `user_id` (alias for `sub`), `expires_at`, plus any extra claims
listed in `expose_claims` that are present in the token.

# Example (TOML)

```toml
[auth.me]
enabled = true
expose_claims = ["email", "tenant_id", "https://myapp.com/role"]
```

enabled.description: Enable the `GET /auth/me` endpoint.  Default: `false` (opt-in).

expose_claims.description:
Raw JWT claim names to include in the response body, beyond the
always-present `sub`, `user_id`, and `expires_at`.

Names must match the raw claim key in the token (e.g. `"email"`,
`"https://myapp.com/role"`).  Claims absent from the token are silently
omitted.  The `user_id` alias for `sub` is always included and must
**not** be listed here — listing `"user_id"` would silently return
nothing because the JWT only carries `sub`.

TrustedIssuer.description:
One additional trusted token issuer (`[[auth.additional_issuers]]`, #1400).

The issuer-level settings of [`OidcConfig`], for a second (third, …) issuer. `issuer`
is mandatory: it is what routes a token here.

issuer.description: The issuer URL, matched exactly against a token's `iss`.

jwks_uri.description: Pinned JWKS endpoint; discovered from `issuer` when unset.

scope_claim.description: Claim scopes are read from; see [`OidcConfig::scope_claim`].

SocialAuthConfig.description:
Social-login provider configuration compiled from `[auth.social]` (#368).

Each configured provider is auto-registered by the server and served through
the account-linking trust gate at `/auth/v1/authorize` / `/auth/v1/callback`.
Only implemented providers are typable: an `[auth.social.apple]` block is a
compile-time unknown-field error, not a silently-ignored table.

redirect_uri_allowlist.description:
Allow-listed `redirect_uri` values for the post-login token hand-off
(#427). Empty (the default) keeps the JSON-token response: the
client-supplied `redirect_uri` is never used as a redirect target, so
there is no open-redirect surface. Non-empty switches the callback to an
implicit-style fragment redirect, refusing any URI not matched here.

apple.description:
Sign in with `Apple`. Configuring it also mounts the `POST` variant of
`/auth/v1/callback` that `Apple`'s `response_mode=form_post` requires.

client_secret_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the client secret.

discovery_url.description:
`OIDC` issuer override (default `https://accounts.google.com`). For
`Google`-compatible stand-ins; the runtime's SSRF guards still apply.

GitHubSocialConfig.description:
`[auth.social.github]` — `GitHub` `OAuth2` social-login client (#368).

`GitHub` serves no `OIDC` discovery document; the endpoints are the fixed
well-known paths under [`base_url`](Self::base_url) /
[`api_base_url`](Self::api_base_url), overridable for `GitHub` Enterprise
Server deployments.

client_secret_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the client secret.

base_url.description:
Web base URL override (default `https://github.com`) — `GitHub` Enterprise
Server. The runtime's SSRF guards still apply.

api_base_url.description:
API base URL override (default `https://api.github.com`) — `GitHub`
Enterprise Server (`https://HOSTNAME/api/v3`).

AppleSocialConfig.description:
`[auth.social.apple]` — Sign in with `Apple` (#943).

`Apple` has no `client_secret_env`: its client secret is an ES256 assertion
the runtime mints from the `.p8` key over
([`team_id`](Self::team_id), [`key_id`](Self::key_id),
[`client_id`](Self::client_id)) and re-mints before expiry. Supply the key
through exactly one of [`private_key_env`](Self::private_key_env) or
[`private_key_path`](Self::private_key_path) — naming both, or neither, is a
configuration error rather than a silent preference.

client_id.description:
The services ID registered with `Apple` (its `OAuth2` `client_id`, and
the `aud` of every `id_token`).

team_id.description: `Apple` developer team ID — the client-secret assertion's `iss`.

key_id.description: Key ID of the `.p8` signing key — the assertion header's `kid`.

private_key_env.description:
Name of the environment variable holding the `.p8` private key, PEM text
and all. Mutually exclusive with
[`private_key_path`](Self::private_key_path).

private_key_path.description:
Filesystem path to the `.p8` private key. Mutually exclusive with
[`private_key_env`](Self::private_key_env).

base_url.description:
Base URL override (default `https://appleid.apple.com`). This is also
the issuer every `id_token` must name, so the two move together. The
runtime's SSRF guards still apply.

DiscordSocialConfig.description:
`[auth.social.discord]` — `Discord` `OAuth2` social login (#944).

`Discord` reports `verified` on the user object, and the runtime honours it:
an unverified address keys on `(discord, id)` rather than on the email. That
check is why `discord` is in the default trusted-email set.

client_secret_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the client secret.

base_url.description:
Base URL override (default `https://discord.com`). The runtime's SSRF
guards still apply.

FacebookSocialConfig.description:
`[auth.social.facebook]` — `Facebook` `OAuth2` social login (#944).

`Facebook` publishes **no** email-verification signal, so every `Facebook`
identity keys on `(facebook, id)` and `facebook` is deliberately absent from
the default trusted-email set. The Graph API version is part of the request
path and `Meta` deprecates versions on a schedule, so it is configuration
rather than a constant.

client_secret_env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the client secret.

base_url.description:
Web base URL override (default `https://www.facebook.com`) — the
authorization dialog. The runtime's SSRF guards still apply.

graph_base_url.description:
Graph API base URL override (default `https://graph.facebook.com`) — the
token and profile endpoints. The runtime's SSRF guards still apply.

LocalAuthConfig.description:
`[auth.local]` — the auth methods `FraiseQL` operates itself, rather than
delegating to an `IdP` (#367).

Every enabled method mounts real `HTTP` routes and requires a database pool:
credentials, `MFA` enrollments, `OTP` budgets and sessions are all durable
state. A method enabled without what it needs refuses to boot rather than
mounting a flow that cannot complete.

password.description:
Email + password sign-in: mounts `/auth/v1/password/{signup,login}` and
the reset pair. Reset-link delivery additionally requires
[`email_from`](Self::email_from).

otp.description:
Email `OTP` / magic-link sign-in: mounts `/auth/v1/otp` and
`/auth/v1/verify`. Requires [`email_from`](Self::email_from) — a code
nobody receives is not a login method.

mfa.description:
`TOTP` `MFA`: mounts `/auth/v1/mfa/{enroll,challenge,verify,unenroll}`,
backed by the Postgres enrollment store (enrollments must survive a
restart, or a deploy locks every user out of their own account).

anonymous.description:
Anonymous guest sessions: mounts `POST /auth/v1/signup`, which issues a
session to any caller with no credentials at all. Off by default — this
is a deliberate "anyone may hold a session" posture, not a convenience.

email_verification.description:
Email verification for local-password accounts (#945): mounts
`POST /auth/v1/email/verify/{start,confirm}`, both of which require an
authenticated caller and act only on that caller's own account.

Requires [`password`](Self::password) — verification proves the address a
*local* identity claims, and an account without one has nothing to verify
— plus [`email_from`](Self::email_from) and
[`verification_url_template`](Self::verification_url_template).

Confirming promotes the account's own `auth.tb_user.email`, which is what
lets a later trusted social sign-in for the same address link into it. It
never merges two accounts: an address already verified elsewhere is
refused.

mfa_issuer.description:
Service name shown in authenticator apps for `MFA` enrollment
(`otpauth://…?issuer=`). Defaults to `"`FraiseQL`"`.

email_from_name.description:
The sender name shown beside [`email_from`](Self::email_from)'s address. Unset sends
the bare address.

email.description:
The subject and bodies of each mail these methods send (`[auth.local.email]`). Unset
keeps the built-in English text. Boxed: every compiled schema carries this struct, and
few carry mail templates.

reset_url_template.description:
Template for the password-reset link, with `{token}` substituted for the
opaque reset token — e.g. `https://app.example.com/reset?token={token}`.
Required when `password` is enabled: the link points at the operator's
front end, which `FraiseQL` cannot guess.

magic_link_template.description:
Template for the `OTP` magic link, with `{token}` substituted for a link
token that signs in alone, and `{code}` for the six-digit code. Optional:
when absent the email carries the bare six-digit code.

otp_allowed_query.description:
`SELECT` deciding who may sign in by `OTP`, with `$email` bound to the normalized
address — e.g. `SELECT 1 FROM tb_member WHERE email = $email AND active`. A row
admits the address; no row or a failed query refuses it. A refused address gets the
same answers as an admitted one, and no mail and no account. Unset admits every
address. It governs `OTP` only: password signup and social sign-in stay open.

verification_url_template.description:
Template for the email-verification link, with `{token}` substituted for
the opaque verification token — e.g.
`https://app.example.com/verify-email?token={token}`. Required when
[`email_verification`](Self::email_verification) is enabled: the link
points at the operator's front end, which `FraiseQL` cannot guess.

session_transport.description: fraiseql.toml: `[auth.local] session_transport` is no longer accepted; write `[auth.session] transport`

LocalEmailConfig.description:
`[auth.local.email]`: the subject and body of each mail `[auth.local]` sends. A kind left
unset keeps the built-in English text.

otp.description: The sign-in mail: its code, and its magic link when `magic_link_template` is set.

EmailTemplate.description:
One mail's subject and bodies.

In `fraiseql.toml` the bodies are files, `text_template` and `html_template`, relative to
the file. `fraiseql compile` reads them into `text` and `html` and drops the paths, so the
server needs only the compiled schema.

subject.description: The subject line, sent as written: no placeholders.

text_template.description: Path of the plain-text body, in `fraiseql.toml` only.

html_template.description:
Path of the `HTML` body, in `fraiseql.toml` only. Sent beside the text body as
`multipart/alternative`.

text.description: [auth.local.email] text is the compiled body of a mail template. In fraiseql.toml, write it in a file and name the file with text_template.

html.description: [auth.local.email] html is the compiled body of a mail template. In fraiseql.toml, write it in a file and name the file with html_template.

SessionConfig.description:
`[auth.session]` — the lifetime of the sessions this server mints (#1853).

Governs password, `OTP`, `MFA`, social and `SAML` sign-in. Anonymous guest
sessions keep their fixed lifetime.

ttl_secs.description:
Lifetime of an access token, in seconds. Unset, each sign-in method keeps
its own lifetime.

absolute_ttl_secs.description:
How long a session can be kept alive by refreshing, in seconds from
sign-in. Setting it mounts `/auth/v1/session/refresh` and
`/auth/v1/session/logout`; unset, neither is mounted.

SessionTransport.description: `[auth.session] transport`: how a session reaches the client.

oneOf.description:
The access and refresh tokens are in the `JSON` response body, for the client to
keep and send as a bearer token.

The access token is in the `__Host-access_token` cookie and the refresh token in
`__Secure-refresh_token`, scoped to `/auth/v1/session`; both are `HttpOnly`,
`Secure` and `SameSite=Strict`, and no response body carries either token.

Requires `[auth.session] absolute_ttl_secs`: without it no logout route is
mounted, and nothing could clear the cookies. A social sign-in also needs
`[auth.social] redirect_uri_allowlist`, and a `SAML` one `[saml]
post_login_redirect_uri`: their cookies are set on the redirect to the front end.

AuthDatabaseConfig.description:
`[auth.database]` — the database first-party auth connects to, as its own role
(#1965).

Every auth table lives in schema `auth`, owned by the role this connection
authenticates as; the engine's own role needs no grant on it. Only the name of the
environment variable holding the URL is compiled: the URL carries credentials.

url_env.description: The environment variable that holds the auth role's connection URL.

pool_min.description: Connections the pool keeps open. Unset: none until needed.

pool_max.description: The most connections the pool opens. Unset: [`Self::DEFAULT_POOL_MAX`].

acquire_timeout_secs.description:
How long a request waits for a connection, in seconds. Unset:
[`Self::DEFAULT_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECS`].

SubscriptionsConfig.description:
WebSocket subscription configuration.

```toml
[subscriptions]
max_subscriptions_per_connection = 50

[subscriptions.hooks]
on_connect = "http://localhost:8001/hooks/ws-connect"
on_disconnect = "http://localhost:8001/hooks/ws-disconnect"
on_subscribe = "http://localhost:8001/hooks/ws-subscribe"
timeout_ms = 500

[subscriptions.capture.tb_ticket]
document_column = "data"
```

max_subscriptions_per_connection.description:
Maximum subscriptions per WebSocket connection.
`None` (or omitted) means unlimited.

capture.description:
How the capture trigger reads each table it sits on, by the table's name as a
type's `subscribable_tables` spells it.

```toml
[subscriptions.capture.tb_ticket]
document_column = "data"
```

max_connections_per_principal.description:
Open WebSocket connections one principal may hold at once, within its tenant.
A positive number or `"unlimited"`; omitted, 32. A further upgrade is refused
with `429 SUBSCRIPTION_CONNECTIONS_EXHAUSTED` until one of them closes.

max_connections_per_tenant.description:
Open WebSocket connections the authenticated principals of one tenant may hold
at once. A positive number or `"unlimited"`; omitted, 1000. A tenant registered
with its own `max_subscription_connections` quota uses that instead.

max_anonymous_connections.description:
Open WebSocket connections with no principal, across the server. A positive
number or `"unlimited"`; omitted, 1000. They never count against a tenant's
or a principal's connections, whatever tenant they name.

max_anonymous_connections_per_ip.description:
Open WebSocket connections with no principal from one client address, read as
the rate limiter reads it (`[security.rate_limiting] trust_proxy_headers` and
`trusted_proxy_cidrs`). A positive number or `"unlimited"`; omitted, 32.

SubscriptionHooksConfig.description: Webhook URLs invoked during subscription lifecycle events.

on_disconnect.description: URL to POST on WebSocket disconnect (fire-and-forget).

on_subscribe.description: URL to POST before a subscription is registered (fail-closed).

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds for fail-closed hooks (default: 500).

CaptureTableConfig.description:
How the capture trigger reads one table (`[subscriptions.capture.<table>]`).

```toml
[subscriptions.capture.tb_ticket]
document_column = "data"
```

document_column.description:
The column the table keeps its entity document in. A captured write is stored as
that document, as a mutation's is, and not as the table's row.

ConnectionCap.description: A positive number of connections, or "unlimited".

ValidationConfig.description:
Query validation limits (depth and complexity).

```toml
[validation]
max_query_depth = 10
max_query_complexity = 100
```

max_query_depth.description: Maximum allowed query nesting depth. `None` uses the server default (10).

max_query_complexity.description: Maximum allowed query complexity score. `None` uses the server default (100).

max_response_bytes.description:
Maximum bytes a single read may deliver, measured on the rows returned.

Depth and complexity score the request; this bounds the answer, which is
the only cost a read from a materialised view actually has. `None` leaves
reads unbounded by size.

max_page_size.description:
Maximum rows a top-level `first`/`last`/`limit` argument may request,
guarding against unbounded-pagination denial of service (#421). `None`
uses the server default (1000); the server also honours the
`FRAISEQL_MAX_PAGE_SIZE` environment variable as an override.

max_offset.description:
The deepest offset a client may page to (#1306): a GraphQL `offset:`, REST
`?offset=` or `?rel.offset=` beyond it is refused before any statement, naming the
relay connection as the path that pages at any depth. `None` (the default) refuses
none; the server also honours `FRAISEQL_MAX_OFFSET` as an override.

max_semi_additive_cells.description:
The most (bucket, entity) cells an aggregate carrying a semi-additive measure forward
may read (#1459): each is one index seek, and a larger request is refused before the
measure is read. `None` uses the runtime default (250,000).

DebugConfig.description:
Debug/development configuration.

Controls features that should only be enabled during development or
in trusted environments. All flags default to off.

```toml
[debug]
enabled = true
database_explain = true
expose_sql = true
```

enabled.description: Master switch — all debug features require this to be `true`.

database_explain.description:
When `true`, the explain endpoint will also run `EXPLAIN` against the
database and include the query plan in the response.

expose_sql.description:
When `true`, the explain endpoint includes the generated SQL in the
response. Defaults to `true` (SQL is shown even without
`database_explain`).

McpConfig.description:
MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configuration: the `[mcp]` table of
`fraiseql.toml`, read by the compiler and compiled into the schema the server reads,
one type at both ends.

enabled.description: Whether MCP is enabled.

transport.description: How the server is reached: `"http"`, `"stdio"`, or `"both"`.

include.description: Whitelist of query/mutation names to expose (empty = all).

exclude.description: Blacklist of query/mutation names to hide.

read_only.description:
**Read-only exposure**: when `true`, no mutation is ever exposed as an MCP
tool, regardless of [`include`](Self::include)/[`exclude`](Self::exclude) —
a fail-closed default for AI callers, so a mutation added later is not
silently exposed. Wins over `include` listing a mutation.

session_state.description:
Keep per-thread working state across an agent's tool calls, in the
`[session_state]` store (#967).

Off by default, and opt-in rather than automatic for two reasons: it
writes to a durable store on every authenticated tool call, and it makes
one call's result depend on the calls before it — which is the point, and
also a behaviour change no deployment should acquire by upgrading.

Requires an authenticated caller and a configured `[session_state]`
backend. With either missing, tool calls run exactly as they do today: an
anonymous caller has no principal to scope a thread to, so there is
nothing safe to key on.

McpTransport.description: How an MCP server is reached.

oneOf.description: Over HTTP, at [`McpConfig::path`].
Over standard input and output, when the server is started as an MCP stdio server.
Both.

RestTomlConfig.description:
REST transport configuration parsed from the `[rest]` TOML section.

All fields have defaults matching `RestConfig::default()` in `fraiseql-core`.
When `enabled` is `false` (the default), the REST transport is not mounted.

Unknown keys are refused. `[rest]` used to accept anything, so a retired key — or a
misspelled one — compiled and was silently the default.

enabled.description: Whether the REST transport is enabled.

path.description: Base URL path for REST endpoints.

default_page_size.description: Default page size when no `?limit=` is specified.

default_embed_page_size.description:
Page each parent row gets of an embedded relationship when the request names none
(`?rel.limit=`). Applied at most at `max_page_size`.

ndjson_batch_size.description: Batch size for NDJSON streaming responses.

max_bulk_affected.description: Maximum affected rows for bulk PATCH/DELETE.

max_filter_bytes.description: Maximum byte length for `?filter=` JSON values.

delete_response.description: How DELETE endpoints report success: `"no_content"` (default) or `"entity"`.

default_cache_ttl.description:
Default result cache TTL in seconds (0 = no caching): the `max-age` of a GET's
`Cache-Control`. An authenticated read (any credential) is `private`; only an
anonymous read is `public`, and only a public one carries `s-maxage`.

require_auth.description: Whether REST endpoints require authentication by default.

sse_max_replay_events.description:
How many delivered events a `Last-Event-ID` resume may reach back over
(0 = no bound; see `RestConfig::sse_max_replay_events`).

include.description: Allowlist of type names to expose as REST resources (empty = all).

exclude.description: Denylist of type names to exclude from REST resources.

etag.description: Whether to enable `ETag` / `If-None-Match` conditional response support.

idempotency_ttl_seconds.description: TTL in seconds for idempotency key deduplication.

max_embedded_reads.description: [rest] max_embedded_reads was removed: a `?select=` embed is no longer a sub-read per parent row but one composed statement, and there are no sub-reads left to count. It is bounded by the request's cost ceiling — set [security.cost_budget] per_request_max (and [validation] max_response_bytes for its bytes) — and each embedded level's page by [rest] default_embed_page_size. Remove the key.

DeleteResponseToml.description:
DELETE response mode for TOML configuration.

Uses lowercase serde names for TOML ergonomics.

oneOf.description: Return `204 No Content`.
Return `200` with the deleted entity in the body.

enabled.description: Whether the gRPC transport is enabled.

reflection.description: Whether to enable gRPC Server Reflection.

ChangelogConfig.description:
Configuration for exposing the observer entity-change log as queryable GraphQL types.

When `expose = true`, the compiler injects two read-only object types
(`EntityChangeLog`, `TransportCheckpoint`), a cursor-paginated list query, a
point-lookup query, and a checkpoint upsert mutation, all backed by the views the
changelog migration installs. Sidecar consumers can then poll the changelog over the
same GraphQL endpoint they use for everything else — same auth, audit, rate limiting.

The generated operations are gated by `read_role` / `write_role` (RBAC). The views
read from `tb_entity_change_log` / `tb_transport_checkpoint`, which the observer
system installs (or which the operator supplies as a documented prerequisite).

expose.description: Master switch. When `false`, no changelog types are registered (default).

schema.description:
PostgreSQL schema holding `tb_entity_change_log` and `tb_transport_checkpoint`.
Default `"core"` (the observer install convention).

read_role.description:
Role required to query the changelog (`entity_change_logs`, `transport_checkpoint`).

Matched against `SecurityContext.roles`. `None` disables the read gate (not
recommended for production). Default `Some("changelog_reader")`.

write_role.description:
Role required to upsert checkpoints (`upsert_transport_checkpoint`).

Matched against `SecurityContext.roles`. `None` disables the write gate.
Default `Some("changelog_writer")`.

max_limit.description:
Maximum rows a single `entity_change_logs` page should return.

Enforced as a documented/runtime clamp rather than a GraphQL argument
constraint (the argument system has no max). Default `1000`.

write_enabled.description:
Whether the mutation executor writes the `tb_entity_change_log` outbox row
in-transaction (the Change-Spine transactional outbox). Default `true`.

Distinct from [`expose`](Self::expose), which gates the *read* path (the
#149 GraphQL changelog types): `write_enabled` gates the *write* path. Set
`false` to disable the outbox write **globally** — e.g. for an application
that does not consume the Change Spine — so no mutation pays the write.
Overridable at runtime by `FRAISEQL_CHANGELOG_ENABLED`; composes (AND) with
the per-mutation
[`MutationDefinition.changelog`](crate::schema::MutationDefinition) flag.

convention.description:
The GraphQL surface's naming convention. Unwritten, a schema document's own
convention stands, and with none the surface is `camelCase`: `snake_case`
columns and functions in the database, `camelCase` operation and field names for
clients, and mutation input keys recased `camelCase` → `snake_case` before they
reach the SQL functions. `"preserve"` keeps names exactly as authored.

acronyms.description:
Acronyms whose internal digit stays attached when a GraphQL field name is mapped
back to its `snake_case` JSONB key (e.g. `s3`, `ipv4`, `oauth2`), added on top of
the engine's built-in defaults. Author the atomic form (`s3`, not `s_3`).

NamingConvention.description:
Naming convention for GraphQL operation names.

Controls how operation names (queries, mutations, subscriptions) are exposed
in the introspection schema and resolved at execution time.

Python/TypeScript SDKs emit `snake_case` operation names (e.g., `create_dns_server`).
Standard GraphQL convention is `camelCase` (`createDnsServer`). This setting
controls whether the compiler/runtime converts names automatically.

oneOf.description: Preserve operation names as authored (`snake_case` from Python, etc.).
Convert operation names to camelCase for GraphQL convention.

auto_error_union.description:
Opt-in: synthesize a shared `MutationError` type and a per-mutation result union
(`<Mutation>Result = Entity | MutationError`) for every object-returning mutation,
rewriting its return type to that union so the server's success/error
discrimination has a union to resolve against. Mutations that already return a
union are left untouched.

CrudNamingConfig.description:
CRUD function naming configuration, compiled from `[crud]` in `fraiseql.toml`.

When a mutation's `sql_source` is absent, the compiler resolves the PostgreSQL
function name using these templates and the entity name derived from the
mutation's `return_type`.

**Precedence** (highest first):
1. Explicit `sql_source` on the mutation — always wins.
2. Per-operation custom template (`create_template`, `update_template`, `delete_template`).
3. Built-in preset (`function_naming = "trinity"`).

`function_schema` is applied as a prefix to the resolved name
(e.g. `"app"` + `"create_user"` → `"app.create_user"`).

function_naming.description: Built-in naming preset (expands to fixed templates).

CrudNamingPreset.description: Built-in CRUD naming preset for automatic `sql_source` resolution.

oneOf.description: Trinity pattern: `create_{entity}` / `update_{entity}` / `delete_{entity}`.

HierarchyConfig.description:
Configuration for a single hierarchy used by ID-based ltree operators.

Defines the database table and ltree path column for a named hierarchy.
The `id` column is always `id` (UUID) per the trinity pattern — not configurable.

table.description: Database table containing the ltree column (e.g., `"tb_category"`).

path_column.description: Name of the ltree column in the table (e.g., `"category_path"`).

SessionVariablesConfig.description:
Top-level session variables configuration in the compiled schema.

When populated, the executor calls `set_config()` before each query and
mutation to inject per-request values (JWT claims, HTTP headers, or literals)
as PostgreSQL transaction-scoped settings.  SQL functions and RLS policies can
then read these via `current_setting('app.tenant_id', true)`.

inject_started_at.description:
Inject the built-in `fraiseql.started_at` timestamp before every mutation (and
only mutations: no read consults it).

SessionVariableMapping.description:
One session variable declaration.

The source is flattened, so a mapping is one flat table in both JSON and TOML:

```toml
[[session_variables.variables]]
name = "app.tenant_id"
source = "jwt"
claim = "tenant_id"
```

Flat is what lets `[session_variables]` be declared in `fraiseql.toml` against
this exact type, rather than through a CLI-side mirror struct — and a mirror
struct at a producer↔consumer seam is how declarations get silently dropped
(#806/#807/#758).

A key the mapping's source does not take is refused, the keys of another source
included: serde cannot deny unknown keys through a flatten, so it is read through
`FlatSessionVariable`, a private enum with one closed table per source.

oneOf.description: Pull from a JWT claim.

claim.description: JWT claim name to look up (e.g. `"sub"`, `"tenant_id"`).

oneOf.description:
Pull from an HTTP request header (gRPC metadata on gRPC). A header is
client-controlled: never use one for row-level security or tenant scoping.
A fixed literal value.

value.description: The literal string value to inject.

oneOf.description:
Pull from a field of the enriched identity the database supplies; a missing field
is an error, never an empty setting.

field.description:
The enriched field name, without the `fraiseql.enriched.` prefix (e.g.
`"actor_role"`).
